name: La Mirande
positioning: Independent hotel in an 18th-century Provencal townhouse at the foot of the Palais des Papes in Avignon, with rooms dressed in historic French printed fabrics, a garden and several restaurants
best_for: Travelers who want to stay beside the Palais des Papes in historic Avignon
Food lovers who want a choice of gourmet restaurant, bistro, tavern and a shared chef's table
Lovers of 18th-century decor, antiques and historic fabrics

facts.text: La Mirande sits at the foot of the Palais des Papes in Avignon.
The hotel is an 18th-century Provencal townhouse.
The Palais des Papes is the world's largest Gothic palace and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Each Deluxe Room has its own colour palette, inspired by the fabric chosen for its wall coverings.
The Grand Deluxe Room bathrooms have built-in bathtubs of Arabescato Carrara marble with Edwardian-inspired fittings.
The Suite is an 18th-century suite set between the gardens and the Palais des Papes.
Chef Michele Donvito took the helm at La Mirande in 2026.
At the gourmet restaurant, the chef builds his menus as triptychs of three dishes that complement one another.
The gourmet restaurant offers a Renaissance dining room or a garden overlooking the Palais des Papes.
Bistrot Pamard serves lunch and dinner in the Louis XV salon beneath Venetian chandeliers, or outdoors facing the Palais des Papes.
Le Mirage serves white, rose and red wines from regional vineyards by the carafe.
The bar's signature creations showcase Chateauneuf-du-Pape wines alongside spirits from Avignon's Manguin Distillery.

highlights.text: Each room is adorned with a historic French printed fabric: Indiennes and Toile de Jouy from the workshops of Braquenie, heirs to the Manufacture Royale de Jouy.

La Table Haute is the historic kitchen, with a 19th-century wood-fired stove, where up to twelve guests sit around a large sycamore table and Chef Thomas Longuesserre prepares a single menu for the whole table.
The garden, created by gardener Marc Leonetti, mixes box hedges, fruit trees, holm oaks, roses and aromatic herbs, all grown according to the principles of organic farming.
The owners cultivate an estate in Sarrians, in the Vaucluse, some twenty kilometres from the hotel, that supplies the kitchens with seasonal produce.
The owners are a music-loving family, and there have always been concerts at La Mirande.

considerations.text: The gourmet restaurant is open Thursday through Sunday only, while Bistrot Pamard is open seven days a week.
Valet parking and pets both carry an additional charge.
WhataHotel notes that the historic building's traditional room layouts may feel compact.
